overall_summary: Analysis of two log chunks revealed a high volume of SSH authentication events, including numerous successful logins for admin and root accounts, alongside multiple failed attempts indicative of potential brute-force activity. Both chunks exhibited abnormal severity assignments for routine events, with successful logins and service starts frequently logged as ERROR or CRITICAL. Kernel network filtering events (connection accept/drop/reject) and HTTP errors on login/admin endpoints were also observed. The overall pattern suggests a possible targeted attack or compromised credentials, though some anomalies may stem from misconfigured logging.

Failed SSH password attempts, possible brute-force.

recurring_patterns.pattern: Successful SSH login events for multiple user accounts (root, admin, service, alice, bob) observed in both chunks.
Kernel network connection filtering events (ACCEPT, DROP, REJECT) appear consistently.
Service start events (nginx, sshd, cron, sudo) logged with elevated severity levels.
Failed SSH password attempts for various users, suggesting possible brute-force activity.
